expected_level_description: You can: - advise the board and executive on the organisation's most significant legal risks - give definitive advice on novel, contentious, or high-value matters - set the organisation's appetite for legal risk - assure the quality of legal advice across the organisation, including external advice

You can: - set the organisation's contracting standards and risk positions - lead negotiations on the most valuable or high-risk agreements - advise senior leaders on strategic commercial arrangements, such as partnerships and joint ventures

You can: - set the organisation's legal position on the use of health and care data - lead on high-risk or novel uses of data, such as research, data platforms, and AI - represent the organisation with regulators on information law

You can: - advise on who owns software, data, and content made by staff, suppliers, and partners - draft licences and intellectual property terms, including open source release of the organisation's code - advise on commercial use of the organisation's data and software, and on sharing benefits

You can: - advise on routes to market, including frameworks, direct awards, and competitive procedures - advise on evaluation, award decisions, and changes to contracts after award - respond to supplier challenges and complaints - advise on subsidy control and competition risks in partnerships

You can: - manage a caseload of disputes and claims from first notice to settlement or hearing - assess the merits and value of claims and recommend strategy - negotiate settlements and use alternative dispute resolution - make sure lessons from claims feed into safety, contract, and service improvements

You can: - advise on the organisation's powers and duties, including when it can provide or commission a service - advise on the regulation of digital health products, such as software as a medical device - liaise with clinical negligence schemes and external lawyers on claims involving digital services - advise on consent, capacity, and patient rights in digital services

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders

You can: - make decisions characterised by medium levels of risk and complexity and recommend decisions as risk and complexity increase - build consensus between services or independent stakeholders - identify problems or issues in the team dynamic and rectify them - engage in varying types of feedback, choosing the right type at the appropriate time and ensuring the discussion and decision stick - bring people together to form a motivated team and help create the right environment for a team to work in - facilitate the best team makeup depending on the situation
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
